chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Rifa'ah ibn Musa said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who touched a girl in the month of Ramadan and emitted semen. He said: 'If it was from a forbidden act, he should seek Allah's forgiveness with the forgiveness of one who never returns, and fast one day in place of one day. And if it was from a permissible act, he should seek Allah's forgiveness and not return, and fast one day in place of one day.'

This is a rare, unusual hadith and contrary to the fatwas of all our scholars. Perhaps the narrator erred in his statement at the end of the report, 'and fast one day in place of one day,' because the content of the report indicates this. Do you not see that he began by distinguishing between emitting semen from a forbidden act and emitting semen from a permissible act? And according to the fatwa he narrated, there is no difference between the two, so it is known that it is an error of the narrator. And whoever has intercourse with his wife and emits semen, what is obligatory upon him is what is obligatory upon one who has intercourse. That which indicates this is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for emitting semen through touching during Ramadan?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi analyzes a rare narration regarding emission during Ramadan, critiquing its internal logic to argue that the penalty should mirror that of full intercourse rather than a simple day-for-day fast. This reflects the Shia scholarly method of reconciling apparent contradictions in hadith by prioritizing coherent legal principles over isolated reports. The discussion underscores the importance of distinguishing between minor and major sexual acts in determining expiation (*kaffarah*) during the holy month.
